back_translation: When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you shall set apart a portion as an offering to the LORD, a holy district of the land 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. This entire district shall be holy all around.
Within this there shall be a section for the sanctuary, a square of 500 by 500 cubits, with 50 cubits of open land around it.
From this holy district you shall measure off a length of 25,000 cubits and a width of 10,000 cubits, and in it shall be the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
This is a holy portion of the land for the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who draw near to minister to the LORD; it shall be a place for their houses and a holy area for the sanctuary.
An adjacent area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple, as their possession for towns to live in.
You shall designate the property of the city, 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, alongside the holy district set apart; it shall belong to the whole house of Israel.

The prince shall have the area on both sides of the holy district and the city's property, flanking the holy district and the city's property, extending from the west side westward and from the east side eastward, equal in length to one of the tribal portions, from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.
This land shall be his possession in Israel, and My princes shall no longer oppress My people, but shall give the rest of the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
Thus says the Lord GOD: Enough, O princes of Israel! Put away violence and oppression, and do justice and righteousness; stop driving My people off their land, declares the Lord GOD.
You shall use honest scales, an honest ephah, and an honest bath.
The ephah and the bath shall be of the same measure, the bath holding a tenth of a homer and the ephah a tenth of a homer; the homer shall be the standard for both.
One shekel shall equal twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels shall equal one mina for you.
This is the offering you shall present: a sixth of an ephah of wheat from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah of barley from each homer of barley.
The prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath, is a tenth of a bath from each cor (a cor equals ten baths or one homer, for ten baths equal a homer).

And one sheep shall be given from each flock of two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel. These are for the grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings, to make atonement for the people, declares the Lord GOD.
All the people of the land must take part in this offering for the prince in Israel.

It shall be the prince's duty to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the feasts, the New Moons, and the Sabbaths, at all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel. He shall provide the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord GOD: On the first day of the first month you shall take an unblemished young bull and purify the sanctuary.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the gateposts of the inner court.
You shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins unintentionally or in ignorance; thus you will make atonement for the temple.
On the fourteenth day of the first month you shall observe the Passover, a feast of seven days, during which unleavened bread shall be eaten.
On that day the prince shall provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
During the seven days of the feast, he shall offer a burnt offering to the LORD—seven bulls and seven unblemished rams daily for seven days—along with a male goat daily as a sin offering.
He shall also provide a grain offering of an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, with a hin of olive oil for each ephah of grain.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, at the feast, he shall make the same provision for seven days—the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil.
